newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian office of Slovenian magazine set ablaze.
newsitem.headline: Austrian office of Slovenian magazine set ablaze.

text.p: Unidentified assailants looted and then set ablaze the Austrian offices of a Slovenian language magazine, days after the publication received an anonymous threat, police said on Wednesday.
A police spokesman said the attackers broke into the offices of the weekly Vestnik in Klagenfurt, about 50 km (30 miles) north of the Slovenian border, in the early hours of Wednesday.

They stole 65,000 schillings ($6,000) in cash and two computers before starting a fire in the building, which also houses the Association of Slovenian Groups. Police assessed the damage at over one million schillings.
"Last Thursday the magazine received a threatening letter...but we are assuming the attack does not have a political motive," the spokesman for Klagenfurt police said.
Marjan Sturm, head of the Association of Slovenian Groups, said he believed the fire may be the work of extremists.
He noted that the first in a series of apparently politically motivated letter bomb attacks began three years ago to the day on Tuesday.
Klagenfurt is the provincial capital of Carinthia, home to most of Austria's Slovenian minority. ($1=11.01 Schilling)
